entries.name: Crimson Fate Heaven Severing Manual
entries.description: Not a scripture. A duelist's notebook that outlived every duelist who added to it, bound in something nobody asks about. To anyone else it is a famous curio and a long list of names. To an Heir of Crimson Fate it is the whole argument.

comprehension.description: The first reading — you stop flinching at your own blood.
Crimson Field Absorption: the ground learns to pour the wrong way.
Mastery: a notebook of duels is a notebook about people, and it has been read.
Heaven Severing Blood: one cut, across everything.
Crimson Blood Frenzy: the line is finished, and the blood keeps drawing it.

entries.name: Myriad Venoms Heaven Devouring Codex
entries.description: Less a manual than a pharmacopoeia with the labels removed, on the theory that a Sovereign already knows and nobody else should. The last third is written in something that is not ink.

comprehension.description: The first reading — you stop reaching for the antidote.
Sovereign's Draught: the field is yours, and it is wet.
Mastery: what the court keeps in jars, this body keeps in its blood.
The dose stops being a dose and becomes a dialect.
Body of Myriad Poison: nothing it touches is clean afterwards.

entries.name: Vajra War God Immortal Scripture
entries.description: A campaign record that stopped recording and started instructing somewhere around the fourth century of it. There is no final page; the compilers appear to have considered the question premature.

comprehension.description: The first reading — a war is a direction, not an event.
Perfect War Body: the guard that lasts as long as it is needed.
Mastery: light thrown at the Front is light the Front keeps.
Eternal War Momentum: what was done to you, read and returned.
Momentum of the Eternal War: every turn standing is a turn harder to end.

entries.name: Sublime Death Sutra
entries.description: A soul manual no library holds and no shop sells, turning up once in a very long while anywhere in the mortal world. To all but one lineage it is a famous curio. To an Envoy of Sublime Death past the threshold it is the whole office, written down.

comprehension.description: The first reading — the sutra stops being a set of words about dying.
Death's Last Bloom: what is nearly spent flowers hardest.
Mastery: spirit sent at the reader finds nothing left to frighten.
Death's Neglect: the office is read whole, and its holder is passed over once.

entries.name: Infinite Echo Scripture
entries.description: Written once and copied never — every surviving version is the same book remembering itself slightly differently. To anyone else it is a famous curio and a long argument about repetition. To one who carries the Echoes it is instructions.

comprehension.description: The first reading — the repetitions stop looking like a copyist's mistake.
The reader learns to hear a blow arriving before it does.
Mastery: mind sent at the reader finds the same mind already there, and stops.
Echo Resonance: the scripture is read whole, and what answers it answers everything.
